newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Assistant Energy Secretary Ervin resigns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Assistant Energy Secretary Ervin resigns.

text.p: The assistant U.S. energy secretary in charge of energy efficiency and renewable energy programs resigned to join the President's Council for Sustainable Development, the Energy Department said Thursday.
Christine Ervin will join the council effective May 1, the department said.
"The Department of Energy has benefited greatly from Christine's service, and I wish her the best in her next endeavor," Energy Secretary Federico Pena said in a statement.
Pena in his statement thanked Ervin for staying on at the department longer "longer than originally intended, to help with the transition and assure continuity for her program."
Cited by industry sources as potential replacements for Ervin are David Nemtzow, president of the Alliance to Save Energy, and Dan Reicher, O'Leary's former chief of staff.
Pena recently named Reicher to be one of his senior advisors.
